audit.whatIsWrong: Row 6 (2+ items) says Warwick on both layers, but whys[6], spikes[3].text and breakdown-late text all say Kassadin flips the matchup once he has items, and the packet chart says Kassadin.
audit.why: Kassadin's Riftwalk drops to 2s at rank 3 and stacks damage on repeat casts; Void Stone reduces the magic damage your passive and Q lean on. The page currently renders 'Warwick wins 2+ items' next to prose saying the opposite.
audit.corrected: Row 6 flipped to Kassadin on both layers as a matched pair, rating lowered to 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: No concrete cooldown numbers anywhere — the packet flags zero sequencing cues.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 falling to 2s at rank 3, so 'trade on Riftwalk's cooldown' is close to meaningless; the real punish cooldown in lane is Force Pulse at 21s rank 1, and your own Infinite Duress is 110s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Put the real numbers into spikes[1].text and phases[4].why: bait Force Pulse (21s at rank 1), then commit; do not spend a 110s ultimate on chip.

audit.whatIsWrong: Infinite Duress is called a 'point-and-click fight starter' in phases[4].why and breakdown.late, and spikes[1].text claims it suppresses him 'through the start of a Riftwalk cast'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Warwick leaps in a direction and suppresses the FIRST champion he collides with for 1.5s — it is a directional leap that can miss, and the kit flags it as an interruptible channel. Nothing in the files supports suppressing him mid-Riftwalk.
audit.corrected: Restated as a directional leap onto the first champion collided with. The reliable framing is that Riftwalk is only 500 range, so land the leap while he is still committed to melee, not as a cast-interrupt claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: Null Sphere's text says it 'interrupts channels' and Warwick's Infinite Duress carries a channel flag. If that interrupt applies, Kassadin has a hard answer to your only lockdown and the page should lead with it.
audit.why: The kit files cannot settle this — 'channel' on Infinite Duress is a derived flag, and suppression is usually implemented as a channel that is immune to ordinary interrupts. I will not assert either direction.
audit.corrected: No text written. Flagged for the user.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Kassadin's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps and suppresses the first champion it collides with for 1.5s. Riftwalk is only 500 range, so leap while he is still committed to melee.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. Kassadin carry threat: 9.5/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion in its path for a 1.5s suppress — line it up, it can miss. Kassadin carry threat: 9.5/10 — shift to picks and wave control once he has items.

edits.before: Your R Infinite Duress suppresses him through the start of a Riftwalk cast — ult the instant he's in range and he can't blink out, turning level 6 into a kill window before he stacks.
edits.after: Infinite Duress leaps onto the first champion it collides with for a 1.5s suppress, and Riftwalk only moves him 500 units — bait Force Pulse (21s at rank 1), then leap on top of him before he has stacks.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Kassadin carry threat 9.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on he flips it: Riftwalk is 2s at rank 3 and Void Stone cuts your magic damage. Kassadin carry threat 9.5/10 — close before this.
